column1: # Jāmiʿ al-ʿUlūm wa-l-Ḥikam — Hadith 36: “Whoever relieves a believer of a hardship”

column2: From Abū Hurayrah (may Allah be pleased with him), from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, who said: “Whoever relieves a believer of one of the hardships of this world,

Allah will relieve him of one of the hardships of the Day of Resurrection. Whoever makes things easy for someone in difficulty, Allah will make things easy for him in this world and the Hereafter. Whoever veils a Muslim, Allah will veil him in this world and the Hereafter.

Allah is in the aid of the servant so long as the servant is in the aid of his brother. Whoever treads a path seeking knowledge in it, Allah will make easy for him thereby a path to Paradise. No people gather in one of the houses of Allah,

reciting the Book of Allah and studying it together, but tranquillity descends upon them, mercy covers them, the angels surround them, and Allah mentions them among those who are with Him. And whoever is slowed down by his deeds will not be hastened by his lineage.” Muslim reported it.

Muslim recorded this hadith through the narration of al-Aʿmash, from Abū Ṣāliḥ, from Abū Hurayrah. More than one of the ḥuffāẓ objected to his recording it, among them Abū al-Faḍl al-Harawī and al-Dāraquṭnī, because Asbāṭ ibn Muḥammad narrated it from al-Aʿmash
with the words: I was told it from Abū Ṣāliḥ. This makes it clear that al-Aʿmash did not hear it from Abū Ṣāliḥ, and he did not name the person who told it to him from Abū Ṣāliḥ.

Al-Tirmidhī and others preferred this narration. Some of al-Aʿmash's students added to the text of the hadith: “And whoever lets a Muslim off a bargain he regrets, Allah will let him off his stumbles on the Day of Resurrection.”
Al-Bukhārī and Muslim recorded in the two Ṣaḥīḥs, from the hadith of Ibn ʿUmar, that the Prophet ﷺ said:

“The Muslim is the brother of the Muslim: he does not wrong him or abandon him to harm. Whoever is meeting his brother's need, Allah is meeting his need. Whoever dispels a Muslim's hardship, Allah will dispel for him one of the hardships of the Day of Resurrection. And whoever veils a Muslim, Allah will veil him on the Day of Resurrection.”
Al-Ṭabarānī recorded, from the hadith of Kaʿb ibn ʿUjrah, that the Prophet ﷺ said: “Whoever relieves a believer of one of his hardships,

Allah will relieve him of one of the hardships of the Day of Resurrection; whoever veils a believer's fault, Allah will veil his fault; and whoever dispels a believer's hardship, Allah will dispel his hardship.”
Imam Aḥmad recorded, from the hadith of Maslamah ibn Mukhallad, that the Prophet ﷺ said: “Whoever veils a Muslim in this world,

Allah will veil him in this world and the Hereafter; whoever rescues someone in distress, Allah will release him from one of the hardships of the Day of Resurrection; and whoever is meeting his brother's need, Allah is meeting his need.”

His words ﷺ, “Whoever relieves a believer of one of the hardships of this world, Allah will relieve him of one of the hardships of the Day of Resurrection,” go back to the principle that the recompense is of the same kind as the deed.
Texts with this meaning are many, such as his words ﷺ: “Allah shows mercy only to the merciful among His servants,” and his words: “Allah punishes those who torment people in this world.”

A hardship (kurbah) is a great distress that plunges the one who suffers it into anguish (karb). Relieving it (tanfīs) means lightening it for him; it is taken from loosening a stranglehold, as though the noose is slackened for him so that he can take a breath. Dispelling it (tafrīj) is greater than that:

it is removing the hardship from him altogether, so that his hardship lifts and his worry and distress are gone. So the recompense for relieving is relief, and the recompense for dispelling is dispelling, as in the hadith of Ibn ʿUmar; and the two are combined in the hadith of Kaʿb ibn ʿUjrah.

Al-Tirmidhī recorded, from the hadith of Abū Saʿīd al-Khudrī, as marfūʿ (attributed to the Prophet ﷺ): “Any believer who feeds a hungry believer, Allah will feed him on the Day of Resurrection from the fruits of Paradise;

any believer who gives drink to a thirsty believer, Allah will give him drink on the Day of Resurrection from the sealed nectar; and any believer who clothes a naked believer, Allah will clothe him in the green garments of Paradise.”
Imam Aḥmad recorded it, with doubt over whether it is marfūʿ, and it has been said that the correct view is that it is mawqūf (stopping short of the Prophet ﷺ).

Ibn Abī al-Dunyā reported, with his chain of narration, from Ibn Masʿūd, who said: “People will be gathered on the Day of Resurrection more naked than they ever were, hungrier than they ever were, thirstier than they ever were and wearier than they ever were.

Whoever clothed others for the sake of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, Allah will clothe him; whoever fed others for the sake of Allah, Allah will feed him; whoever gave others drink for the sake of Allah, Allah will give him drink; and whoever spared others for the sake of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, Allah will spare him.”

Al-Bayhaqī recorded, from the hadith of Anas, as marfūʿ: “A man of the people of Paradise will look down on the people of the Fire on the Day of Resurrection, and a man of the people of the Fire will call out to him: So-and-so, do you know me?
He will say: No, by Allah, I do not know you. Who are you?

He will say: I am the one you passed by in the world and asked for a drink of water, and I gave you a drink. He will say: Now I know you. He will say: Then intercede for me with your Lord by it. So he will ask Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, saying: Let me intercede for him; and He will give the command concerning him, and he will be brought out of the Fire.”

He said, “one of the hardships of the Day of Resurrection,” and did not say “of this world and the Hereafter,” as he did with making things easy and with veiling. By way of explaining this, it has been said that hardships are great distresses,

and not everyone meets with them in this world, unlike difficulty and faults that need veiling, from which hardly anyone in this world is free, if only through some important needs becoming hard to meet.

It has also been said that the hardships of this world, compared with those of the Hereafter, are as nothing, so Allah has stored up with Himself the recompense for relieving hardships, to relieve the hardships of the Hereafter with it. This is shown by the words of the Prophet ﷺ:

“Allah will gather the first and the last on one plain; the caller will make them hear, sight will reach all of them, and the sun will draw near them. People will reach a degree of grief and anguish they cannot bear or endure, and they will say to one another: Do you not see what has befallen you?
Will you not look for someone to intercede for you with your Lord?” And he mentioned the hadith of intercession. Al-Bukhārī and Muslim recorded it with this meaning from the hadith of Abū Hurayrah.

They recorded, from the hadith of ʿĀʾishah, that the Prophet ﷺ said: “You will be gathered barefoot, naked and uncircumcised.” She said: I said: Messenger of Allah, men and women looking at one another?
He said: “The matter will be too grave for that to concern them.”

They recorded, from the hadith of Ibn ʿUmar, from the Prophet ﷺ, concerning His words, “The Day when mankind will stand before the Lord of the worlds” [al-Muṭaffifīn 83:6]: “One of them will stand in his sweat up to the middle of his ears.”
They recorded, from the hadith of Abū Hurayrah, that the Prophet ﷺ said: “People will sweat on the Day of Resurrection until their sweat goes seventy cubits into the earth,

and it will bridle them, reaching their ears.” The wording is al-Bukhārī's. Muslim's wording is: “The sweat will go seventy fathoms into the earth, and it will reach people's mouths,” or “their ears.”
Muslim recorded, from the hadith of al-Miqdād, that the Prophet ﷺ said: “The sun will draw near to the servants until it is the distance of a mile or two, and the sun will melt them,
and they will be in sweat according to their deeds: some it will reach to their heels, some to their knees, some to their waists, and some it will bridle completely.”

Ibn Masʿūd said: The whole earth will be fire on the Day of Resurrection, with Paradise beyond it, its goblets and its maidens in view. A man will sweat until his sweat seeps into the earth to the depth of a man's height, then rises until it reaches his nose, though the reckoning has not yet touched him. Someone said: From what is that, Abū ʿAbd al-Raḥmān?
He said: From what he sees being done to people.
Abū Mūsā said: The sun will be above people's heads on the Day of Resurrection, and their deeds will either shade them or leave them exposed to it.
In the Musnad, from the hadith of ʿUqbah ibn ʿĀmir, as marfūʿ: “Every man will be in the shade of his charity until judgement is passed between people.”
His words ﷺ: “Whoever makes things easy for someone in difficulty, Allah will make things easy for him in this world and the Hereafter.”

This too shows that difficulty can occur in the Hereafter. Allah has described the Day of Resurrection as a difficult day, not easy for the disbelievers, which shows that it is easy for others. He says:
“And it will be a difficult day for the disbelievers” [al-Furqān 25:26].
Making things easy in this world for someone in difficulty over money takes one of two forms. One is giving him time until he is in ease, which is obligatory, as the Exalted says:

“And if [the debtor] is in hardship, then [let there be] respite until ease” [al-Baqarah 2:280]. The other is remitting the debt, if one is his creditor, or otherwise giving him what will end his difficulty. Both carry great merit.

In the two Ṣaḥīḥs, from Abū Hurayrah, the Prophet ﷺ said: “There was a merchant who used to lend to people. Whenever he saw someone in difficulty, he would say to his servants: Let him off, so that perhaps Allah will let us off. And Allah let him off.”
In both of them, from Ḥudhayfah and Abū Masʿūd al-Anṣārī, who heard the Prophet ﷺ say: “A man died and was asked [what he had done]. He said: I used to trade with people,

and I would let off the well-off and make things light for the one in difficulty.” In one narration he said: “I used to give time to the one in difficulty and be lenient over the coin” — or he said: “over the payment” — “and he was forgiven.”
Muslim recorded it from the hadith of Abū Masʿūd, from the Prophet ﷺ.
In his hadith: “Allah said: We are more entitled to that than he is; let him off.”

He also recorded, from the hadith of Abū Qatādah, that the Prophet ﷺ said: “Whoever would be pleased for Allah to save him from the hardships of the Day of Resurrection, let him relieve someone in difficulty, or remit his debt.”

He also recorded, from the hadith of Abū al-Yasar, that the Prophet ﷺ said: “Whoever gives time to someone in difficulty, or remits his debt, Allah will shade him in His shade on the Day when there is no shade but His.”
In the Musnad, from Ibn ʿUmar, the Prophet ﷺ said: “Whoever wants his supplication to be answered and his hardship removed, let him bring relief to someone in difficulty.”
His words ﷺ: “Whoever veils a Muslim, Allah will veil him in this world and the Hereafter.”
Texts with this meaning are many.

Ibn Mājah recorded, from the hadith of Ibn ʿAbbās, that the Prophet ﷺ said: “Whoever veils the fault of his Muslim brother, Allah will veil his fault on the Day of Resurrection; and whoever exposes the fault of his Muslim brother, Allah will expose his fault until He disgraces him by it in his own house.”
Imam Aḥmad recorded, from the hadith of ʿUqbah ibn ʿĀmir, that he heard the Prophet ﷺ say:
“Whoever veils a believer's fault in this world, Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, will veil him on the Day of Resurrection.”

It has been narrated that one of the Salaf said: I knew people who had no faults, but they spoke of people's faults, so people spoke of faults in them. And I knew people who had faults, but they held back from people's faults, so their own faults were forgotten — or words to that effect.
This is borne out by the hadith of Abū Barzah, from the Prophet ﷺ, that he said: “O you who have believed with your tongues while faith has not entered your hearts, do not backbite the Muslims,

and do not pursue their faults; for whoever pursues their faults, Allah will pursue his faults, and whoever's faults Allah pursues, He will disgrace him in his own house.” Imam Aḥmad and Abū Dāwūd recorded it, and al-Tirmidhī recorded its meaning from the hadith of Ibn ʿUmar.
Know that people are of two types.
The first is someone whose conduct is veiled, who is not known for any acts of disobedience. If a lapse or a slip occurs from him, it is not permissible to expose it,
to lay it bare or to talk about it, because that is unlawful backbiting. It is about this that the texts have come, and concerning it Allah the Exalted has said:
“Those who love that indecency should spread among the believers will have a painful punishment in this world and the Hereafter” [al-Nūr 24:19].

What is meant is spreading indecency about a believer whose conduct is veiled, whether over something he did or something he was accused of while innocent of it, as in the story of the Slander (al-ifk).

One of the righteous viziers said to someone who enjoined what is right: Strive to veil the sinners, for their sins coming to light is a blemish on the people of Islam, and the most fitting course is to veil faults. Likewise if such a person came repentant and remorseful

and confessed to something that incurs a prescribed punishment, without specifying it, he would not be asked to specify it; rather he would be told to go back and veil himself, as the Prophet ﷺ told Māʿiz and the Ghāmidī woman, and as the man who said, “I have done something that incurs a prescribed punishment, so carry it out on me,” was not asked to specify.
Likewise if he is caught in his crime and it has not reached the ruler, intercession is made for him so that it does not reach the ruler.
It is about cases like this that the hadith from the Prophet ﷺ came: “Overlook the slips of people of standing.”
Abū Dāwūd and al-Nasāʾī recorded it from the hadith of ʿĀʾishah.
The second is someone notorious for acts of disobedience, who commits them openly and cares neither what he commits nor what is said to him. This is the open sinner,

and speaking of him is not forbidden backbiting, as al-Ḥasan al-Baṣrī and others stated explicitly. There is no harm in looking into the affairs of such a person, so that the prescribed punishments may be carried out on him.
Some of the scholars of our [Ḥanbalī] school stated this explicitly, citing the words of the Prophet ﷺ: “Go, Unays, to this man's wife, and if she confesses, stone her.”

No intercession is made for such a person when he is caught, even if it has not reached the ruler; rather he is left until the prescribed punishment is carried out on him, so that his evil is checked and others like him are deterred by it.
Mālik said: For someone not known to harm people, who has simply had a slip, there is no harm in interceding for him so long as it has not reached the ruler.

But as for someone known for evil or corruption, I would not like anyone to intercede for him; rather he should be left until the prescribed punishment is carried out on him. Ibn al-Mundhir and others related this.
Imam Aḥmad disliked reporting sinners to the ruler in any case. He disliked it only

because rulers mostly do not carry out the prescribed punishments in the proper way. That is why he said: If you know that he will carry out the prescribed punishment on him, report him. Then he mentioned that they had flogged a man and he died — meaning that killing him was not permissible.
If someone of the first type repents, it is best for him to repent between himself and Allah the Exalted and to veil himself.
As for the second type, some said that the same applies, and others said that it is better for him to go to the ruler and confess to what incurs a prescribed punishment, so that it purifies him.

His words, “Allah is in the aid of the servant so long as the servant is in the aid of his brother”; and in the hadith of Ibn ʿUmar: “Whoever is meeting his brother's need, Allah is meeting his need.”
The merit of meeting people's needs and striving to meet them has already been discussed in the commentary on the twenty-fifth and twenty-sixth hadiths.
Al-Ṭabarānī recorded, from the hadith of ʿUmar, as marfūʿ: “The best of deeds is bringing joy to a believer: you clothe his nakedness, or satisfy his hunger, or meet a need for him.”

Al-Ḥasan al-Baṣrī sent some of his companions to meet a man's need, and said to them: Pass by Thābit al-Bunānī and take him with you. They came to Thābit, and he said: I am in spiritual retreat (iʿtikāf).
They went back to al-Ḥasan and told him, and he said: Tell him: O bleary-eyed one, do you not know that your walking to meet your Muslim brother's need is better for you than one Ḥajj after another?
They went back to Thābit, and he left his retreat and went with them.
Imam Aḥmad recorded, from the hadith of a daughter of Khabbāb ibn al-Aratt, who said: Khabbāb went out with a raiding party,
and the Prophet ﷺ used to look in on us, even milking a she-goat of ours into a bowl of ours until it overflowed. When Khabbāb came back he milked it, and its milk went back to what it had been.

Abū Bakr al-Ṣiddīq (may Allah be pleased with him) used to milk the sheep of the people of his quarter. When he became caliph, one of their girls said: Now he will not milk them for us. Abū Bakr said: Indeed I will, and I hope that what I have taken on will not change me from anything I used to do — or words to that effect.
They used to take on the milking
because among the Arabs the women did not milk; they considered it disgraceful. So when the men were away, the women needed someone to milk for them.
It is narrated that the Prophet ﷺ said to some people: “Do not give me milk to drink that a woman has milked.”

ʿUmar used to look after widows, drawing water for them at night. Ṭalḥah saw him at night going into a woman's house, so Ṭalḥah went in to her by day and found that she was a blind, crippled old woman. He asked her: What does this man do for you?

She said: For such-and-such a time he has been looking after me, bringing me what I need and taking away the filth from me. Ṭalḥah said: May your mother be bereaved of you, Ṭalḥah! Is it ʿUmar's slips you are pursuing?
Abū Wāʾil used to go round the women and old women of his quarter every day, buying them what they needed and what would be of use to them.
Mujāhid said: I accompanied Ibn ʿUmar on a journey to serve him, and he used to serve me.
Many of the righteous used to stipulate with their companions on a journey that they would serve them.
A man accompanied some people on jihād and stipulated with them that he would serve them. Whenever one of them wanted to wash his head or his garment, he would say:

This is part of my condition — and he would do it for him. He died, and when they stripped him for washing they saw written on his hand: Of the people of Paradise. They looked closely, and it was writing between the skin and the flesh.
In the two Ṣaḥīḥs, from Anas, who said: We were with the Prophet ﷺ on a journey; some of us were fasting and some were not. We stopped at a halting place on a hot day.

The one of us with the most shade was the one who had a cloak, and some of us shielded ourselves from the sun with our hands. Those who were fasting collapsed, while those not fasting got up, pitched the tents and watered the mounts. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “Those who were not fasting have taken the reward today.”

It is narrated from a man of Aslam that the Prophet ﷺ was brought food on one of his journeys. He ate of it and his companions ate, but the man of Aslam held back his hand. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to him: “What is the matter with you?”
He said: I am fasting. He said: “What led you to do so?”
He said: I have my two sons with me, who saddle my mount and serve me. He said: “They will always have the advantage over you, then.”
In the Marāsīl of Abū Dāwūd, from Abū Qilābah: some of the Companions of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ came back praising a companion of theirs.
They said: We have never seen anyone like so-and-so: whenever we were travelling he was reciting, and whenever we stopped he was praying. He said: “Then who used to see to his needs?”
— and so on, until he mentioned: “And who used to feed his camel, or his mount?”
They said: We did. He said: “Then all of you are better than he is.”
His words ﷺ: “Whoever treads a path seeking knowledge in it, Allah will make easy for him thereby a path to Paradise.”
Abū al-Dardāʾ also narrated this meaning from the Prophet ﷺ. Treading a path to seek knowledge includes treading an actual path,

that is, walking on foot to the gatherings of scholars; and it includes treading the figurative paths that lead to the attainment of knowledge, such as memorising it, studying it, discussing it with others, reading it, writing it, seeking to understand it, and similar figurative paths by which knowledge is reached.

His words, “Allah will make easy for him thereby a path to Paradise,” may mean that Allah makes easy for him the knowledge he has sought and whose path he has trodden, and smooths it for him; for knowledge is a path leading to Paradise. This is like His words, Exalted is He: “And We have certainly made the Qurʾān easy to remember; so is there anyone who will be reminded?” [al-Qamar 54:17].
One of the Salaf said: Is there any seeker of knowledge, that he may be helped in it?

It may also mean that Allah makes it easy for the seeker of knowledge, if by seeking it he intends the Face of Allah, to benefit from it and act according to it, so that it becomes a cause of his guidance and, through that, of his entering Paradise.

Allah may also make easy for the seeker of knowledge other kinds of knowledge that benefit him and lead to Paradise, as has been said: Whoever acts on what he knows, Allah gives him knowledge of what he did not know;

and as has been said: The reward of a good deed is the good deed that follows it. This is shown by His words, Exalted is He: “And Allah increases in guidance those who are guided” [Maryam 19:76], and His words: “And those who are guided, He increases them in guidance and grants them their taqwā” [Muḥammad 47:17].
It may also include making easy the tangible path to Paradise on the Day of Resurrection — the Bridge (al-ṣirāṭ) — and the terrors before it and after it.
These are made easy for the seeker of knowledge who benefits from it, for knowledge leads to Allah by the shortest of paths to Him. Whoever treads its path and does not turn aside from it

reaches Allah the Exalted and Paradise by the shortest and easiest of paths, and all the paths that lead to Paradise are made easy for him in this world and the Hereafter. There is no path to knowing Allah, to reaching His good pleasure,

to winning nearness to Him and being near Him in the Hereafter, except through the beneficial knowledge with which Allah sent His messengers and sent down His Books. It is what points to Him, and by it one is guided through the darknesses of ignorance, doubt and uncertainty. That is why Allah called His Book a light,
because one is guided by it in the darknesses.

Allah the Exalted says: “There has come to you from Allah a light and a clear Book, by which Allah guides those who pursue His good pleasure to the ways of peace, and brings them out of the darknesses into the light by His permission, and guides them to a straight path” [al-Māʾidah 5:15–16].
The Prophet ﷺ likened those who carry the knowledge he brought to the stars by which one is guided in the darknesses. In the Musnad, from Anas,

the Prophet ﷺ said: “The likeness of the scholars on earth is that of the stars in the sky, by which one is guided in the darknesses of land and sea; when the stars are blotted out, the guides are likely to go astray.”

So long as knowledge remains on earth, people are on guidance, and knowledge remains as long as those who carry it remain. When those who carry it and uphold it are gone, people fall into misguidance, as in the two Ṣaḥīḥs, from ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿAmr,

from the Prophet ﷺ, who said: “Allah does not take away knowledge by snatching it from people's breasts; rather He takes it away by taking the scholars. When no scholar remains, people take ignorant leaders; they are asked and give fatwas without knowledge, so they go astray and lead others astray.”
One day the Prophet ﷺ mentioned the lifting of knowledge, and he was asked: How can knowledge go when we have read the Qurʾān and taught it to our women and our children?
The Prophet ﷺ said: “Here are the Torah and the Gospel with the Jews and the Christians; what use are they to them?”

ʿUbādah ibn al-Ṣāmit was asked about this hadith, and said: If you wish, I will tell you the first knowledge to be lifted from people: humility (khushūʿ). ʿUbādah said this only because knowledge is of two kinds.

The first is that whose fruit is in a person's heart: knowledge of Allah the Exalted, His names, His attributes and His acts, which brings about fear of Him, awe of Him, reverence for Him and submission to Him, as well as love for Him, hope in Him, calling on Him, reliance on Him

and the like. This is beneficial knowledge, as Ibn Masʿūd said: Some people recite the Qurʾān and it does not go beyond their collarbones; but when it falls into the heart and settles firmly in it, it benefits.
Al-Ḥasan said: Knowledge is of two kinds: knowledge on the tongue, which is Allah's proof against the son of Ādam; and knowledge in the heart, which is beneficial knowledge.
The second kind is knowledge on the tongue, which is Allah's proof, as in the hadith:

“The Qurʾān is a proof for you or against you.” The first knowledge to be lifted is beneficial knowledge — the inward knowledge that mingles with hearts and sets them right — while the knowledge of the tongue remains as a proof. People make light of it

and do not act according to it, neither those who carry it nor anyone else. Then this knowledge goes with the passing of those who carry it, until nothing remains but the Qurʾān in its written copies, with no one there who knows its meanings,
its limits or its rulings. Then at the end of time it is taken away by night, so that nothing of it at all remains, either in the copies or in hearts; and after that the Hour will come,
as he ﷺ said: “The Hour will come only upon the worst of people,” and he said: “The Hour will not come while there is anyone on earth saying: Allah, Allah.”

His words ﷺ: “No people gather in one of the houses of Allah, reciting the Book of Allah and studying it together, but tranquillity descends upon them, mercy covers them, the angels surround them, and Allah mentions them among those who are with Him.”
This shows that it is recommended to sit in the mosques to recite the Qurʾān and study it together.
If this is understood as learning and teaching the Qurʾān, there is no disagreement that it is recommended. In Ṣaḥīḥ al-Bukhārī, from ʿUthmān, the Prophet ﷺ said:
“The best of you is the one who learns the Qurʾān and teaches it.”
Abū ʿAbd al-Raḥmān al-Sulamī said: That is what has kept me sitting in this seat of mine. He had taught the Qurʾān from the time of ʿUthmān ibn ʿAffān until that of al-Ḥajjāj ibn Yūsuf.

If it is understood more generally than that, it includes gathering in the mosques to study the Qurʾān in any form. The Prophet ﷺ would sometimes tell someone to recite the Qurʾān so that he could listen to his recitation,

as he told Ibn Masʿūd to recite to him, saying: “I love to hear it from someone else.” ʿUmar used to tell someone to recite to him and his companions while they listened: sometimes he would tell Abū Mūsā, and sometimes ʿUqbah ibn ʿĀmir.
Ibn ʿAbbās was asked: Which deed is best?

He said: The remembrance of Allah. No people sit in one of the houses of Allah, taking up the Book of Allah together and studying it, but the angels shade them with their wings, and they are the guests of Allah so long as they keep at it, until they move on to some other talk.
It has been narrated as marfūʿ, but the mawqūf version is more authentic.

Yazīd al-Raqāshī reported from Anas, who said: When they had prayed the dawn prayer, they would sit in circle after circle, reciting the Qurʾān, learning the obligations and the sunnahs, and remembering Allah, the Mighty and Majestic.
ʿAṭiyyah reported from Abū Saʿīd al-Khudrī that the Prophet ﷺ said: “No people pray the dawn prayer and then sit in their place of prayer, taking up the Book of Allah together

and studying it, but Allah appoints angels over them who seek forgiveness for them until they move on to some other talk.” This indicates that it is recommended to gather after the dawn prayer to study the Qurʾān, but ʿAṭiyyah has some weakness.
Ḥarb al-Kirmānī reported, with his chain of narration, from al-Awzāʿī, that he was asked about group study after the dawn prayer, and said:
Ḥassān ibn ʿAṭiyyah told me that the first to introduce it in the mosque of Damascus was Hishām ibn Ismāʿīl al-Makhzūmī, in the caliphate of ʿAbd al-Malik ibn Marwān, and people took it up.

With his chain, from Saʿīd ibn ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz and Ibrāhīm ibn Sulaymān: they used to study the Qurʾān together after the dawn prayer in Beirut, while al-Awzāʿī was in the mosque and did not object to them.
Ḥarb mentioned that he saw the people of Damascus, Ḥimṣ, Makkah and al-Baṣrah gathering to recite after the dawn prayer.

The people of al-Shām, however, would all recite a portion of one sūrah together in loud voices, while the people of Makkah and al-Baṣrah would gather and one of them would recite ten verses while the others listened, then another would recite ten, until they finished.
Ḥarb said: All of that is good and fine.
Mālik objected to this practice of the people of al-Shām.

Zayd ibn ʿUbayd al-Dimashqī said: Mālik ibn Anas said to me: I have heard that you sit in circles reciting. I told him what our people used to do, and Mālik said: The Emigrants and the Anṣār were here among us, and we do not know of this. I said: This is Ṭarīf's way?
— and Ṭarīf was a man who would recite with people gathered round him. He said: This is not in accordance with our view.

Abū Muṣʿab and Isḥāq ibn Muḥammad al-Farwī said: We heard Mālik ibn Anas say: Gathering early in the morning after the dawn prayer to recite the Qurʾān is an innovation. Neither the Companions of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ

nor the scholars after them did this. When they had prayed, each would go off on his own, reciting and remembering Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, and then they would leave without speaking to one another, occupied with the remembrance of Allah. All these things are newly introduced.

Ibn Wahb said: I heard Mālik say: Reciting in the mosque was not part of people's practice of old; the first to introduce it in the mosque was al-Ḥajjāj ibn Yūsuf. Mālik said: And I dislike this reciting from a copy of the Qurʾān in the mosque.
Abū Bakr al-Naysābūrī reported all this in his book Manāqib Mālik (may Allah have mercy on him).

Most scholars took as evidence that gathering to study the Qurʾān is recommended in general the hadiths showing that gathering for remembrance is recommended, the Qurʾān being the best kind of remembrance. In the two Ṣaḥīḥs, from Abū Hurayrah, the Prophet ﷺ said:

“Allah has angels who go about the roads seeking the people of remembrance. When they find people remembering Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, they call out to one another: Come to what you are seeking! And they surround them with their wings up to the lowest heaven. Their Lord asks them — and He knows best about them —: What are My servants saying?
They say: They are glorifying You, magnifying You, praising You and extolling You. He says: Have they seen Me?
They say: No, by Allah, they have not seen You. He says: How would it be if they saw Me?
They say: If they saw You, they would be more intense in worshipping You, more intense in extolling and praising You, and more abundant in glorifying You. He says: Then what are they asking of Me?
They say: They are asking You for Paradise. He says: Have they seen it?
They say: No, by Allah, our Lord, they have not seen it. He says: How would it be if they saw it?
They say: If they saw it, they would be more eager for it, more intense in seeking it and greater in their longing for it. He says: From what do they seek refuge?
They say: From the Fire. He says: Have they seen it?
They say: No, by Allah, our Lord, they have not seen it. He says: How would it be if they saw it?

They say: If they saw it, they would flee from it more intensely and fear it more. Allah the Exalted says: I call you to witness that I have forgiven them. One of the angels says: Among them is so-and-so, who is not one of them; he came only for some need of his. He says: They are the company whose companion is never made wretched.”
In Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim, from Muʿāwiyah: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ came out to a circle of his Companions and said: “What has made you sit here?”
They said: We sat to remember Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, and to praise Him for guiding us to Islam and favouring us with it. He said: “By Allah, did nothing make you sit but that?”

They said: By Allah, nothing made us sit but that. He said: “I did not ask you to swear because I suspected you; but Jibrīl came to me and told me that Allah the Exalted is boasting of you to the angels.”

Al-Ḥākim recorded, from the hadith of Muʿāwiyah, who said: I was with the Prophet ﷺ one day, and he entered the mosque and found some people sitting in the mosque. The Prophet ﷺ said: “What has made you sit here?”

They said: We prayed the obligatory prayer, then sat to remind one another of the Book of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, and the Sunnah of His Prophet ﷺ. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “When Allah mentions something, the mention of it becomes great.”
There are many other hadiths with this meaning.

He ﷺ told us that the recompense of those who sit in a house of Allah studying the Book of Allah is four things. The first is that tranquillity descends upon them. In the two Ṣaḥīḥs, from al-Barāʾ ibn ʿĀzib, who said:

A man was reciting Sūrat al-Kahf with a horse beside him. A cloud covered him and began to circle and draw near, and his horse began to shy away from it. In the morning he came to the Prophet ﷺ and told him about it, and he said: “That was tranquillity, which came down for the Qurʾān.”
Also in both of them, from Abū Saʿīd: While Usayd ibn Ḥuḍayr was reciting one night in his date-drying yard, his horse suddenly reared. He recited,
and it reared again; he recited, and it reared again. Usayd said: I was afraid it would trample Yaḥyā — meaning his son. He said: So I went over to it,
and there was something like a canopy above my head, with what looked like lamps in it, rising into the sky until I could no longer see it. In the morning he went to the Prophet ﷺ
and told him about it, and he ﷺ said: “Those were the angels listening to you. Had you kept reciting, by morning people would have seen them, not hidden from them.” The wording of both is Muslim's.

Ibn al-Mubārak reported from Yaḥyā ibn Ayyūb, from ʿUbaydullāh ibn Zaḥr, from Saʿd ibn Masʿūd, that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was in a gathering. He raised his gaze to the sky, then lowered it, then raised it again.
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ was asked about that, and he said: “These people were remembering Allah the Exalted” — meaning

the people of a gathering in front of him — “and tranquillity came down upon them, carried by the angels like a dome. When it drew near them, one of them spoke falsehood, and it was lifted from them.” This is mursal.
The second is that mercy covers them. Allah the Exalted says: “Indeed, the mercy of Allah is near to those who do good” [al-Aʿrāf 7:56].
Al-Ḥākim recorded, from the hadith of Salmān, that he was among a band of people remembering Allah the Exalted, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ passed by them and said: “What were you saying?
For I saw mercy descending upon you, and I wanted to share in it with you.”

Al-Bazzār recorded, from the hadith of Anas, that the Prophet ﷺ said: “Allah has roving bands of angels who seek out circles of remembrance. When they come upon them, they surround them, then send their leader up to the heaven, to the Lord of Might, Blessed and Exalted is He, and they say:

Our Lord, we came upon servants of Yours who glorify Your blessings, recite Your Book, send blessings upon Your Prophet, and ask You for their Hereafter and their world. Blessed and Exalted is He, He says:

Cover them with My mercy. They say: Our Lord, among them is so-and-so, the great sinner, who only attached himself to them. The Exalted says: Cover them with My mercy, for they are the company whose companion is never made wretched.”

The third is that the angels surround them. This is mentioned in the hadiths we have cited, and in the hadith of Abū Hurayrah given earlier: “And they surround them with their wings up to the lowest heaven.”
In a narration of Imam Aḥmad's: “Some of them rise above others until they reach the Throne.”

Khālid ibn Maʿdān said, tracing it back to the Prophet ﷺ: “Allah has angels in the air, roaming between heaven and earth seeking remembrance. When they hear people remembering Allah the Exalted, they say: Hold on — may Allah give you more! And they spread their wings around them until their words rise up to the Throne.”
Al-Khallāl recorded it in his book al-Sunnah.
The fourth is that Allah mentions them among those who are with Him. In the two Ṣaḥīḥs, from Abū Hurayrah, the Prophet ﷺ said: “Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, says:

I am as My servant thinks of Me, and I am with him when he remembers Me. If he remembers Me within himself, I remember him within Myself; and if he remembers Me in a gathering, I remember him in a gathering better than theirs.”
These four things belong to all who gather to remember Allah the Exalted, as in Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim, from Abū Hurayrah and Abū Saʿīd,

both from the Prophet ﷺ, who said: “Those who remember Allah the Exalted have four things: tranquillity descends upon them, mercy covers them, the angels surround them, and the Lord mentions them among those who are with Him.”

Allah the Exalted has said: “So remember Me; I will remember you” [al-Baqarah 2:152]. Allah's remembrance of His servant is His praising him in the highest assembly among His angels, His boasting of him to them, and His making his name renowned.
Al-Rabīʿ ibn Anas said: Allah remembers whoever remembers Him, gives more to whoever thanks Him, and punishes whoever is ungrateful to Him. And He, the Mighty and Majestic, has said:

“O you who believe, remember Allah with much remembrance, and glorify Him morning and evening. It is He who sends blessings upon you, as do His angels, to bring you out of the darknesses into the light” [al-Aḥzāb 33:41–43].
Allah's blessing (ṣalāh) upon His servant is His praising him among His angels and making his name renowned. So said Abū al-ʿĀliyah, and al-Bukhārī mentioned it in his Ṣaḥīḥ.

A man said to Abū Umāmah: I saw in a dream as though the angels were sending blessings upon you whenever you came in, whenever you went out, whenever you stood and whenever you sat. Abū Umāmah said: And you too, if you wished,

would have the angels send blessings upon you. Then he recited: “O you who believe, remember Allah with much remembrance, and glorify Him morning and evening. It is He who sends blessings upon you, as do His angels” [al-Aḥzāb 33:41–43]. Al-Ḥākim recorded it.
His words ﷺ, “And whoever is slowed down by his deeds will not be hastened by his lineage,” mean that it is deeds that bring the servant to the ranks of the Hereafter,

as the Exalted says: “And for all there are ranks according to what they did” [al-Anʿām 6:132; al-Aḥqāf 46:19]. Whoever is held back by his deeds from reaching the high stations with Allah the Exalted

will not be hastened by his lineage so as to reach those ranks; for Allah the Exalted has made recompense depend on deeds, not on lineage, as the Exalted says: “Then when the Trumpet is blown, there will be no lineage between them that Day, nor will they ask about one another” [al-Muʾminūn 23:101].

Allah the Exalted has commanded that one hasten to His forgiveness and mercy by deeds, as He says: “And hasten to forgiveness from your Lord and a Paradise as wide as the heavens and the earth, prepared for the God-fearing, who spend in ease and in hardship, and who restrain their anger…” — the two verses [Āl ʿImrān 3:133–134]; and He says:

“Indeed, those who are apprehensive out of fear of their Lord, and those who believe in the signs of their Lord, and those who do not associate anything with their Lord, and those who give what they give while their hearts are fearful because they will return to their Lord — it is they who hasten to good deeds, and they are foremost in them” [al-Muʾminūn 23:57–61].

Ibn Masʿūd said: Allah will give the command for the Bridge, and it will be laid over Hell. People will pass over it according to their deeds, group after group: the first of them like a flash of lightning, then like the passing of the wind,
then like the passing of birds, then like the passing of cattle, until a man passes running, and a man passes walking, until the last of them passes dragging himself on his belly, and he says:
My Lord, why did You slow me down?
He says: I did not slow you down; it was your deeds that slowed you down.

In the two Ṣaḥīḥs, from Abū Hurayrah, who said: When there was sent down to him, “And warn your nearest kinsfolk” [al-Shuʿarāʾ 26:214], the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “People of Quraysh, buy yourselves from Allah; I cannot avail you anything against Allah. Sons of ʿAbd al-Muṭṭalib,
I cannot avail you anything against Allah. ʿAbbās ibn ʿAbd al-Muṭṭalib, I cannot avail you anything against Allah. Ṣafiyyah, aunt of the Messenger of Allah,
I cannot avail you anything against Allah. Fāṭimah bint Muḥammad, ask me for whatever you wish; I cannot avail you anything against Allah.”

In a narration outside the two Ṣaḥīḥs: “My allies among you are the God-fearing. Let it not be that people come with deeds while you come to me with the world, carrying it on your necks, and say: Muḥammad! And I say: I have conveyed.”
Ibn Abī al-Dunyā recorded, from the hadith of Abū Hurayrah, that the Prophet ﷺ said: “My allies on the Day of Resurrection are the God-fearing,

even if one lineage is closer than another. People will come with deeds, and you will come with the world, carrying it on your necks, saying: Muḥammad, Muḥammad! And I will say: Like this, and like this” — and he turned away to either side.
Al-Bazzār recorded, from the hadith of Rifāʿah ibn Rāfiʿ, that the Prophet ﷺ said to ʿUmar: “Gather your people for me” — meaning Quraysh. So he gathered them,

and he said: “My allies among you are the God-fearing. If you are those, well and good; if not, then take heed: let it not be that people come with deeds on the Day of Resurrection while you come with burdens, and you are turned away from.”
Al-Ḥākim recorded it in abridged form and graded it authentic.

In the Musnad, from Muʿādh ibn Jabal: When the Prophet ﷺ sent him to Yemen, he went out with him, giving him counsel. Then he turned and faced Madīnah, and said: “The people closest to me are the God-fearing, whoever they are and wherever they are.”

Al-Ṭabarānī recorded it with the addition: “These people of my household think that they are the people closest to me, but it is not so. My allies among you are the God-fearing, whoever they are and wherever they are.”
All this is borne out by what is in the two Ṣaḥīḥs from ʿAmr ibn al-ʿĀṣ: he heard the Prophet ﷺ say:
“The family of Abū so-and-so are not my allies; my ally is only Allah and the righteous among the believers.” He was indicating that his alliance is not attained by lineage,

however close, but only by faith and righteous deeds. Whoever is more complete in faith and deeds has the greater alliance with him, whether or not he is closely related to him. On this meaning one poet says:
By your life, a man is nothing but his religion, / so do not abandon taqwā, relying on lineage.
Islam raised up Salmān of Persia, / and shirk brought low the wretched Abū Lahab.
